design: docs/mechanics/GYM_INTERIORS.md (accepted in principle, docs/STATE.md); its Q1 section holds the measured template geometry this file rests on
note: Shell geometry is NEVER authored here. Every gym's shell box, and therefore every world coordinate below, is derived from that gym's donor record in data/placements.json (position, size, rotation, anchor_mode) through the same transform tools/place_donor.py box() and tools/place_town.py rotate() use. The only measured numbers copied into this file are the template-relative cells recorded by the Q1 read (the healing machine and the trainer spawner); they are recorded as expectations and the healer removal does not depend on them.

measured.source: docs/mechanics/GYM_INTERIORS.md, section 'Q1 ANSWERED (2026-09-29)', read from COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31.zip in memory. The block maps are not committed (no-redistribution); only these measurements are.
measured.shape: every gym is one oval chamber: entrance one end, healing machine and chest the other, one rctmod:trainer_spawner in the middle, 160-248 standable roofed cells of undivided floor, and no second storey

small_gym_relative.why: template-relative, before rotation. The same fitout is stamped in the same relative place in all seven small gyms.

measured.checked_offline: all eight healer cells and all eight spawner cells, mapped through their own placement's rotation, land inside their own shell's box (tools/gym_interiors_audit.py)

healers.decision: the owner, 2026-09-29: no healing machine in any gym. Towns have Centres; a gym with no healer makes its trainers attrition, which is how mainline works.
healers.how: post-placement overwrite, never a template override. One `fill <shell box> <replacement> replace cobblemon:healing_machine` per gym, run after the donor step (tools/reapply.py R16E). Overriding the Cobbleverse template NBT is refused on licence (docs/STATE.md), and the templates are placed by resource id, so the only lawful removal is to write over the placed building - the same thing tools/town_dressing.py does to the towns.
healers.why_a_fill_and_not_a_setblock: the fill is driven by the shell box alone, which is derived from data/placements.json. It removes every healing machine in the shell wherever it stands, so a one-block error in the Q1 measurement cannot leave one behind. The measured cell is recorded per gym as `expect_at` and the audit asserts it lies inside the fill box; it drives nothing.
healers.why_not_air: the healer stands against the chamber's back wall beside the chest. Air leaves a hole in the furniture line; a cut stone of the gym town's own palette reads as the plinth the machine was taken off.
healers.known_consequence: cobblers_blackout's blackout/healer_use advancement fires on any cobblemon:healing_machine, so a gym healer could have been a respawn checkpoint. Measured here, it was one in exactly one gym: blackout/checkpoint/healer_used only sets a checkpoint when the player stands inside a Pokemon Centre's 48-block box (tools/blackout_pack.py checkpoints()), and only Surge's gym healer is inside its town Centre's box (dx 46, dz 35). The other seven fired the advancement and set nothing. Removing all eight removes that one checkpoint, which is what the owner wants: you should not be able to return into a gym you were knocked out of. The trigger is block-type-generic, so nothing dangles.

rules.min_cover_why: a carved room's ceiling block must be at least this many blocks under the heightmap's ground (tools/ground.py, rounded), so no room breaks the surface
rules.min_rock_between_rooms_why: two rooms that are not joined by a declared opening keep at least this much rock between them
rules.max_fall_why: contract G3: no gym route may kill. A fall longer than this must land on minecraft:hay_block, which takes 80% off the damage
rules.sight_margin_why: docs/mechanics/GYM_INTERIORS.md section 3, from data/mansion_guardians.json: a trainer's forceBattleMaxDistance must reach no standable cell outside its own room, less this margin
rules.max_submerged_run_why: contract G2. Blocks travelled along the route with the head under water before a surface or a floor. Gym 2 is the second badge, so no player crossing it has Surf or Dive (docs/mechanics/WATER_MAP.md: Surf and Dive are trained later), and vanilla air is 300 ticks. Fourteen blocks is about six seconds at unaided swim speed, and every flooded stretch in gyms 2, 4 and 7 is shorter than that or is crossed at the surface

spawn_condition_blocks.why: a block that IS a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json, written anyway, inside one gym only. The rule: it must be declared in that gym's own `spawn_condition_blocks` and every cell of it must lie inside that gym's data/spawn_suppression.json box in x/z, which is contract G1 - the zone takes every cell it touches out of every compiled spawn file (tools/compile_spawns.py spawn_free_zones), all y, so no condition inside it can draw anything. docs/mechanics/GYM_INTERIORS.md section 2 says the same of Koga's carpet, and Q8 asked for exactly this test.
spawn_condition_blocks.only: minecraft:water, in gyms 2, 4 and 7. minecraft:sand, minecraft:magma_block and every carpet stay out: none of the three is needed, and magma hurts a standing player, which contract G3 forbids.
spawn_condition_blocks.audited_by: tools/gym_interiors_audit.py (`blocks`): an undeclared spawn condition is a problem, and a declared one written outside the gym's spawn-free box is a problem.

blocks.why: every block any gym generator may write. Vanilla 1.21.1 only. None is a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json except minecraft:water, which is declared per gym under `spawn_condition_blocks` and checked cell by cell against the gym's spawn-free box (the audit reads spawn_blocks.json itself). minecraft:sand is deliberately absent: it is a spawn condition and nothing here needs it.

The two ways to make the works compulsory are named in the report: measure the door and add a zone, or remove the template's spawner with the same post-placement fill and place a persistent kanto_brock at the head of the works (verified on staging 2026-09-24 that a persistent kanto_brock anywhere awards the badge, docs/STATE.md). mechanism.why_this_one: docs/mechanics/GYM_INTERIORS.md section 4: Misty's first draft was three sluice levers, which is Surge's breaker board again, so it was replaced with a current the player rides and cannot switch. What is built here is that current, made out of geometry: a one-way fall in, a surface swim across, and a choice of three shafts out.
mechanism.deviation: the design's soul-sand up-columns are not built. A bubble column is one-way upward, and a one-way upward shaft at the race's head would let a player who took a wrong mouth get stuck at its top. The true mouth is a plain water shaft swum up in six blocks, and the false ones are sumps. Gym 7's geyser is the one bubble column in the six, where being unable to swim back down is the point.
